question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay that wins over mutable config and blocks weakening writes, or keep immutable baseline handling in Policy/Nix-style conformance surfaces?
rationale: The choice changes a security boundary and config precedence contract, and current main only has adjacent conformance checks, Nix-mode immutability, and agent write guards.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, write-conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

options.title: Keep conformance-only policy
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy, policy compare, attestations, and declarative/Nix-managed config for audit while runtime config remains the mutable source of truth.

options.title: Defer for hook design
options.body: Keep this open while related policy hook proposals settle whether enforcement belongs in plugin hooks, core config/write paths, or both.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, write-conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the issue and authored the prior exact implementation candidate, making them the clearest decision owner for the security-boundary direction.
